appPort.description: Legacy: publishes container ports on the host, like docker run -p. Unlike forwardPorts it cannot be changed without a rebuild - prefer forwardPorts.

build.description: Build the image from a Dockerfile instead of pulling one. Mutually exclusive with image and dockerComposeFile.

args.description: Build arguments, passed as --build-arg key=value. Each one must have a matching ARG in the Dockerfile.

cacheFrom.description: Images to pull layers from as a build cache, as docker build --cache-from. Usually a registry image a CI job pushed.

context.description: Directory docker build runs from, relative to devcontainer.json. Paths in COPY and ADD resolve against it. Format: directory

dockerfile.description: Path to the Dockerfile, relative to devcontainer.json. The only required field of the build block.

options.description: Extra flags passed straight to docker build for anything the fields above do not cover.

target.description: Stage to stop at in a multi-stage Dockerfile, as docker build --target.

capAdd.description: Linux capabilities to grant the container, such as SYS_PTRACE for attaching a debugger.

containerEnv.description: Environment variables baked into the container at creation time, visible to every process. Changing one requires a rebuild.

containerUser.default: root, or the last USER instruction in the Dockerfile
containerUser.description: User the container itself is started with, entrypoint included.

customizations.description: Tool-specific configuration, one sub-object per tool. Unknown tools are ignored rather than rejected.
examples:
customizations:
  vscode:
    extensions:
      - golang.go
    settings:
      editor.formatOnSave: true

extensions.description: Extension IDs installed only in Codespaces, on top of the vscode list.

settings.description: Settings applied only when the container runs as a GitHub Codespace.

plugins.description: JetBrains plugin IDs installed when the container is created, in reverse-domain form.

examples:
vscode:
  extensions:
    - golang.go
  settings:
    editor.formatOnSave: true

extensions.description: Extension IDs installed when the container is created, in publisher.name form.

settings.description: Default settings written into the container's workspace settings.json. Users can still override them locally.

devices.description: Host devices to expose inside the container, as docker run --device values. A Docker passthrough, not part of the devcontainer specification.

dockerComposeFile.description: Docker Compose file(s) used to start the services. Later files override earlier ones. Mutually exclusive with image and build.

dockerFile.$comment: use the build block instead: build.dockerfile
dockerFile.description: Path to a Dockerfile. Deprecated shorthand for build.dockerfile - prefer the build block for new configs.

features.description: Dev Container Features to install, keyed by feature ID. An empty object takes the feature's defaults.

forwardPorts.description: Ports forwarded from the container to the local machine. Each entry is a port number (0-65535) or a "host:port" string naming another Compose service.

hostRequirements.description: Minimum host hardware. Codespaces picks a machine type from this; locally it is a pre-flight check.

gpu.description: GPU requirement: true, false, "optional" to use one when present, or an object with cores (at least 1) and memory.
examples:
gpu: true

# Or with specific requirements:
gpu:
  cores: 2
  memory: 4gb

memory.description: Minimum memory. A whole number with an optional lowercase unit: kb, mb, gb, or tb. A bare number means bytes.

storage.description: Minimum free disk space, in the same format as memory.

image.description: Docker image used to create the container. Mutually exclusive with build and dockerComposeFile.

init.description: Pass docker run --init, adding a tiny PID 1 that reaps zombie processes.

initializeCommand.description: Runs on the HOST, before the container is created or started - the only lifecycle command that does. Use it to prepare files the build needs.
examples:
initializeCommand: echo initializing

# Named parallel commands:
initializeCommand:
  setup: ./scripts/setup.sh
  check: ./scripts/check.sh

mounts.description: Extra mounts set up when the container is created. Each entry is a Mount object or a raw docker --mount string.

source.description: Host path for a bind mount, or the volume name for a volume mount. Omit it for tmpfs.

target.description: Absolute path the mount appears at inside the container. Format: directory

type.description: Mount type. bind maps a host path, volume uses a named Docker volume that survives rebuilds. tmpfs is a Docker extension, not part of the specification.

name.description: Name for the dev container, displayed to the user by the IDE.

onCreateCommand.description: First command run inside the container, during creation. In prebuild-capable tools this is the last step baked into the prebuilt image.

otherPortsAttributes.description: Fallback attributes for every forwarded port that portsAttributes does not match.

elevateIfNeeded.description: Ask for elevated privileges when the local port needs them - ports below 1024 such as 22, 80 and 443.

label.description: Name shown next to the port in the IDE's forwarded-ports list.

onAutoForward.description: What happens when a port is auto-forwarded: notify shows a toast, openBrowser opens the system browser, openPreview uses the IDE's built-in browser, silent forwards quietly, and ignore skips the port entirely.

protocol.description: Scheme the IDE uses when it builds the URL for this port.

requireLocalPort.description: Insist on the same port number locally. When false the IDE silently maps to a free port instead; when true it warns that the port is taken.

overrideCommand.default: true for image/Dockerfile, false for Docker Compose
overrideCommand.description: Replace the image's default command with an infinite sleep so the container stays up for the IDE to attach to.

overrideFeatureInstallOrder.description: Force the install order of features by listing their IDs. Without it the order comes from each feature's own installsAfter property.

elevateIfNeeded.description: Ask for elevated privileges when the local port needs them - ports below 1024 such as 22, 80 and 443.

label.description: Name shown next to the port in the IDE's forwarded-ports list.

onAutoForward.description: What happens when this port is auto-forwarded: notify shows a toast, openBrowser opens the system browser every time, openBrowserOnce only the first time in a session, openPreview uses the IDE's built-in browser, silent forwards quietly, and ignore skips the port entirely.

protocol.description: Scheme the IDE uses when it builds the URL for this port.

requireLocalPort.description: Insist on the same port number locally. When false the IDE silently maps to a free port instead; when true it warns that the port is taken.

portsAttributes.description: Per-port forwarding behaviour. Keys are quoted port numbers ("3000"), ranges ("40000-55000"), or regular expressions matching a port.
examples:
portsAttributes:
  "3000":
    label: Web App
    onAutoForward: openBrowser

postAttachCommand.description: Runs each time a tool attaches to the container, so it can fire several times for one container.

postCreateCommand.description: Runs once the container is created and every feature is installed - the usual place to install project dependencies.

postStartCommand.description: Runs every time the container starts, including after a stop/start cycle. Keep it quick - the IDE waits on it.

privileged.description: Pass docker run --privileged, giving the container full access to the host. Prefer capAdd for a specific capability.

remoteEnv.description: Environment variables for processes the IDE spawns, resolved at attach time rather than build time. The only place ${containerEnv:VAR} works; ${localEnv:VAR} reads the host environment.

remoteUser.default: the user the container runs as, often root
remoteUser.description: User the IDE and every process it spawns run as. Does not change the container's own entrypoint user - see containerUser.

runArgs.description: Extra arguments passed to docker run. Ignored for Docker Compose configs, where the Compose file owns the runtime settings.

runServices.description: Additional Compose services started and stopped alongside the primary service. Defaults to every service in the file.

description.description: What the secret is for. Shown next to the input when the IDE prompts for its value.
examples: description: Personal access token for the registry

documentationUrl.description: Link shown alongside the prompt, pointing at instructions for obtaining the value.

secrets.description: Secrets the container needs, keyed by environment variable name (letters, digits and underscore, not starting with a digit). The IDE prompts for the values - none of them are stored in this file.
examples:
secrets:
  MY_TOKEN:
    description: Personal access token for the registry
    documentationUrl: https://example.com/tokens

securityOpt.description: Values for docker run --security-opt, most often seccomp=unconfined so a debugger can attach.

service.description: Service in the Docker Compose file the IDE attaches to - the primary container of the dev environment. Required when dockerComposeFile is set.

shutdownAction.default: stopContainer for image/Dockerfile, stopCompose for Docker Compose
shutdownAction.description: What happens to the container when the IDE disconnects. Use none to leave it running. stopCompose is the Docker Compose counterpart of stopContainer.

updateContentCommand.description: Runs after onCreateCommand, and again whenever the workspace content is refreshed. The default stage waitFor waits on.

updateRemoteUserUID.description: On Linux, update the container user's UID/GID to match the local user so bind-mounted files keep the right ownership.

userEnvProbe.description: Shell used to probe the user's environment variables on container start. A login shell picks up /etc/profile and ~/.profile; an interactive one picks up ~/.bashrc.

waitFor.description: Lifecycle stage the IDE waits for before it reports the container ready and opens the workspace.

watch.description: File-watch configuration for automatic process restarts inside the container.

restart.description: Glob patterns that trigger a restart of the watched process when a matching file changes. Quote them - a leading * is not valid unquoted YAML.

waitFor.description: Lifecycle commands that must finish before file watching starts, so a rebuild does not race the watcher.

workspaceFolder.default: the automatic source-code mount location; "/" for Docker Compose
workspaceFolder.description: Path the IDE opens inside the container. Supports ${localWorkspaceFolderBasename} and the other devcontainer variables. Format: directory

workspaceMount.description: Overrides the default workspace mount, as a docker run --mount string. Set it together with workspaceFolder.
